children: The United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees opposed the proposed sale of a majority stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax, calling for an immediate suspension of the process and a comprehensive review under parliamentary scrutiny.
The forum said the decision was ill-timed and lacked adequate justification, arguing that volatile market conditions called for caution, transparent valuation and wider public deliberation.
Speaking to PTI Videos, IDBI Bank Officers Association President Surav Kumar said, "There is no reason for the sale of our bank specially to the foreign player."

IDBI Banks proposed privatisation is the culmination of a process that began after the lender ran into serious financial trouble. In May 2017, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) placed it under the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework because of weak capital adequacy, poor asset quality and losses. Its net non-performing assets had exceeded 13% in March 2017.

In early 2019, the Life Insurance Corporation of India acquired a 51% controlling stake in IDBI, becoming its largest shareholder. The RBI subsequently classified the lender as a private-sector bank for regulatory purposes. After the banks financial position improved, the central bank lifted the PCA restrictions in March 2021, subject to conditions and continued monitoring.

On October 14, the Cabinet approved Fairfax as the strategic buyer of 60.72% of IDBI for a consideration of Rs 52,878 crore. The government has defended the valuation process, saying independent professional agencies assessed the bank using the market multiple and asset valuation methods. It has also argued that IDBIs volatile share price was not a reliable standalone benchmark.

The IDBI sale has triggered a public exchange between Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. Gandhi has backed the banks employees and questioned why the government wants to sell a lender that has returned to profit. He contrasted the Congress-era establishment of banks with the current government's decision to sell them, and has also raised concerns about employees service conditions, pensions and the impact of privatisation on reservation policies.

Sitharaman hit back, accusing the Congress of treating banks as personal entities and pressuring them to lend to favoured business groups. She argued that politically influenced lending contributed to IDBIs earlier bad-loan problems and said the Modi government had revived the bank through recapitalisation and improved management. IDBI Bank unions have called a strike on November 2 and 3 against government's move to sell its stake<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/>
